name: Whiplash line
summary: A long S-shaped line whose curve changes along its length, drawn from a plant stem; it joins structure and ornament in one stroke.
how: Draw each line as an S-curve with a radius that changes along its length.
Swell the stroke from 1 to 4 units along the curve, as a stem thickens at the base.
Join letters, frame and plant forms with the same line; leave no straight edge to break the flow.
Use few colours, 2 to 4, in muted tones.

origin.note: Victor Horta uses curved iron stems on the stair and the ceiling of the Hotel Tassel.

adoptions.via: Hermann Obrist shows the Cyclamen wall hanging, an embroidery of one long curved stem.
Jugend and Pan magazines print initials and vignettes in interlaced curved lines.
Otto Eckmann draws the Eckmann-Schrift with brush-like curved strokes.
Hector Guimard designs the iron entrances of the Paris Metro with plant-like curves.
